newsitem.title: USA: Louis Dreyfus Q1 up sharply on better prices.
newsitem.headline: Louis Dreyfus Q1 up sharply on better prices.

text.p: Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp said on Monday that its record first quarter net income of $14.0 million, or $.50 per share, up from $2.3 million, $0.08 per share was due to higher commodity prices and a $5.5 million gain from the sale of a property.
Total revenue was $61.1 million, up from $39.9 million a year ago, while cashflow from operating activities before working capital changes rose 67 percent to $30.4 million from $18.2 million.

Natural gas prices rose 29 percent from a year ago to $2.74 per thousand cubic feet and crude oil 23 percent to $22.26 per barrel, while natural gas output rose six percent to 15.5 billion cubic feet and oil fell to 423 thousand barrels.

"Higher oil and gas commodity prices significantly boosted our earnings and operating cash flow results. Earnings were also aided by the sale of a non-core West Texas waterflood property in January 1997," Mark Monroe, chief executive said in a statement with earnings.
The company said that it had succesfully completed 42 out of 44 wells drilled in the quarter.

"The company has increased its drilling activity for the second quarter of 1997, with an average of 10 operated rigs running during the month of April and 13 planned for May, compared to an average of seven operated rigs during the first quarter," Monroe said. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
